summary: Sri Anirvan (1896–1978) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He completed his studies at Sanskrit College and University (~1912–1916), the University of Calcutta (~1916–1918), and the University of Dhaka.
Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan (1932–2019) was an Indologist who earned his Dr. phil. at the University of Hamburg (~1961–1967). He later served there as Privatdozent für Indologie from 1973 to 1997.

Srisa Chandra Vasu (1861–1918) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at Rang Mahal Mission High School and Government College University, Lahore (BA, ~1877–1881), worked as a Vakil at Allahabad High Court (~1888–1893), and was a Fellow at the University of Allahabad.

Stacey Van Vleet specializes in Tibetology, history and archaeology, and Sinology. She studied at the University of Colorado Boulder (MA), at Columbia University (PhD, attested 2006), and under Carole McGranahan and Tashi Tsering Josayma, later holding an attested post at Columbia in 2013.

Stamford Raffles (1781–1826) worked in history, archaeology, and linguistics. He served with the East India Company (~1795–1824) and founded the Zoological Society of London in 1825, serving as its president in 1826.

Stanislas Julien (1797–1873) was a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at the Lycée Pothier and Collège de France under Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat, later holding chairs at the Collège de France (from 1821/1832–1873) and INALCO (1863–1871).

Stanislav Grof (born 1931) studied at Charles University (~1951–1956). His career included posts at Kosmonosy, National Institute of Public Health, Psychiatrické centrum Praha, Johns Hopkins University (1967–1969), Maryland Psychiatric Research Center (1969–1973), Esalen Institute (1973–1987), and CIIS (1994–2015).

Stanisław Schayer (1899–1941) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. In 1922, he founded and became a professor at the University of Warsaw, and was later a member of the Warsaw Scientific Society and Polish Academy of Arts and Sciences.
Stanley Abe is a scholar in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology who held attested academic posts at Duke University in 1995 and 2004.

Stanley Insler (1937–2019) was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. Educated at Columbia, Tübingen, and Yale (under Paul Thieme), he served as Yale's Edward E. Salisbury Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Philology (~1980–2012).

Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah (1929–2014) was a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Ceylon, Cornell University (PhD), and Harvard. He held academic posts at Ceylon (1955–1960), Cambridge (1963–1973), Chicago (1973–1976), and Harvard (1976–2001).

Stanley Lombardo (born 1943) works in philosophy and other fields. He studied at Loyola University New Orleans, Tulane University, and the University of Texas at Austin, and held a faculty post at the University of Kansas from ~1976 to 2014.

Stanley Weinstein (1929–2017) was a Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology scholar. Educated at Komazawa, Tokyo, and Harvard, he taught at Komazawa, SOAS/University of London (~1962–1968), and Yale University, where he was appointed Emeritus Professor in 1968.

Stanley Wolpert (1927–2019) was a scholar of Indology and history. After studying at the City College of New York and the University of Pennsylvania, he served at the University of California, Los Angeles, rising from assistant professor (1959) to department chair (1967).
Stefan Anacker (1939–2021) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He completed his studies at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1964–1970) under Alex Wayman.

Stefan Baums is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics who completed his dissertation at the University of Washington (~2002–2009). He held positions at the University of Copenhagen, University of Munich, Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities, and Göttingen Academy.

Stefan Larsson is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at Stockholm University by 2009 under Per-Arne Berglie, Erik af Edholm, and David Germano, and was a postdoctoral fellow at UC Berkeley in 2012.

Stefan M. Maul (born 1958) is an Assyriologist and historian who studied at Göttingen and Freie Universität Berlin. He held posts at FU Berlin, became Ordinarius at Heidelberg University in 1995, and joined the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities in 2004.

Stefania Travagnin is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. She served as an assistant professor and centre director at the University of Groningen (~2013–2020) before joining SOAS University of London in 2020.

Stefano Zacchetti (1968–2020) was a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar educated at Venice, Sichuan, and Leiden. He held posts at Padua, Soka University (2001–2005), Ca' Foscari Venice (from 2005), and Oxford (2012–2020) as Numata Professor and Balliol College fellow.
